MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

This neuron has no clean semantic trigger; it fires weakly on the last token of a noun/verb phrase that is immediately followed by a modifier or complement (relative "who/that", agentive "by", infinitival "to"), e.g. "spent by", "auditors who", "made by", "order to" — and the same structural slot can also strongly suppress it, so it looks like a low-amplitude, phrase-boundary/continuation-position neuron rather than a concept detector.

L25·N5783unmasked layer
This neuron gives weak, diffuse activation on "glue" tokens sitting mid-phrase just before a multi-word proper name or continued list item — determiners/conjunctions/commas ("the" before *Convention Center*/*Hangzhou National Animation Industry Base*, "and", ","), plus adverbial "notably" and the word-final subword "-vascular"; the mirror-image prepositions/adverbs before names ("on World Cafe", "of view", "finally", closing ")") drive it negative, so it looks like a surface-form/position feature rather than a semantic one.

L27·N12421unmasked layer

Fires on locally surprising/awkward continuation tokens — e.g. the first sub-word piece of a foreign place name ("Cart"-agena, "S"-ardina), an unexpected connective or suffix mid-sentence (" from" after "happy", " mainly", "-ing"), or a comma after a version string — rather than on any coherent semantic category; it appears to track low-predictability tokens (and is suppressed on highly predictable ones like " long high-waisted skirts", " my jacket", " Cool Whip").
